1. Core Clinical Tension: A 35-year-old male with regular travel to rural southern India presents with new-onset generalized seizure, marked leukocytosis, and a solitary ring-enhancing lesion in the left basal temporal lobe lacking the classic pathognomonic scolex or mural nodule on MRI. The central diagnostic tension is distinguishing an atypical degenerating parasitic cyst from intracranial tuberculoma, fungal abscess, or primary intracranial neoplasm.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission evaluation concludes after emergent CT and contrast-enhanced MRI brain scans define the solitary ring-enhancing temporal lesion and baseline triage labs are drawn, prior to send-out serologic testing, surgical craniotomy, and brain tissue molecular analysis.
3. Differential Distinctions: Intracranial tuberculoma is highly prevalent in travelers from South Asia and produces ring-enhancing lesions with granulomatous inflammation, but demonstrates acid-fast bacilli or positive mycobacterial PCR. High-grade glioma or metastatic disease causes solitary ring-enhancing masses with vasogenic edema, but reveals malignant cytology on histological analysis rather than epithelioid granulomatous inflammation. Fungal granulomas (e.g., cryptococcoma) typically show fungal elements on Gomori methenamine silver staining.
case_prompt:
A 35-year-old male born in Tamil Nadu, India, who had emigrated to Singapore six years earlier, presented to the emergency department following a first-onset generalized seizure witnessed by his wife. The episode consisted of generalized jerking movements of all four extremities, upward eye deviation, and loss of consciousness lasting approximately 10 minutes, followed by 10 minutes of postictal confusion and amnesia. He reported no preictal aura, headaches, or antecedent constitutional symptoms such as fevers, night sweats, anorexia, or weight loss. He reported returning to rural India annually, where he frequently visited farms housing livestock, consumed local food, and drank well water. He had no known history of chronic illness or contact with individuals with chronic respiratory infections.

On physical examination, his temperature was 37.8°C, heart rate 76 beats/min, blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air. Neurological examination revealed intact cranial nerves, normal motor strength and sensation throughout, symmetric reflexes, and no focal deficits or meningeal signs.

Laboratory evaluation revealed leukocytosis with a white blood cell count of 18.4 × 10^9/L without peripheral eosinophilia. Serum electrolytes, renal function tests, and liver function panels were normal. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) screening was nonreactive.

Non-contrast head CT revealed an ill-defined 8-mm hypodense lesion with a hyperdense rim in the left basal temporal region, accompanied by mild surrounding vasogenic edema. Contrast-enhanced brain MRI characterized this abnormality as a solitary ring-enhancing lesion measuring 1.2 × 1.0 cm with thick, smooth peripheral enhancement; however, no distinct mural nodule or scolex was visualized.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Intracranial tuberculoma / Central nervous system tuberculosis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading differential given the patient's demographic origin, leukocytosis, solitary ring-enhancing temporal lesion, and intraoperative finding of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, which initially prompted empiric antituberculous therapy. However, acid-fast stains and GeneXpert MTB/RIF testing on brain tissue were repeatedly negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: In view of nonspecific histologic and radiologic features, no definite diagnosis was made at this point. As histology showed granulomatous inflammation, and tuberculosis is endemic in the region, empiric combination ant-tuberculous therapy and a tapering corticosteroid regimen were initiated after discussion and shared decision-making between the patient and medical team while awaiting further diagnostic tests.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: High-grade glial neoplasm or brain metastasis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because a new-onset adult seizure accompanied by a solitary ring-enhancing parenchymal mass with surrounding vasogenic edema frequently represents a primary high-grade glioma or metastatic lesion. However, surgical excision revealed inflammatory exudate and chronic granulomatous inflammation without neoplastic cellular proliferation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: After discussion with the managing neurosurgical team, the patient opted for brain biopsy for definitive diagnosis, in view of the broad range of differential diagnoses based on the neuroradiologic features.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although imaging and initial histology lacked a visible larva or scolex, molecular analysis of the excised brain lesion by species-specific PCR and sequencing confirmed Taenia solium mitochondrial DNA (99.6% identity), supported by positive send-out serum cysticercosis ELISA, definitively establishing neurocysticercosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A Taenia solium-specific PCR targeting the pTsol9 repeat element... and a pan-Cestoda PCR targeting a fragment of the mitochondrial ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA - 12S rRNA) genes... showed 99.6% similarity (805/808) with sequence [AB086256], and thus ascertained that detected DNA was from T. solium.

editor_comments: Atypical solitary ring-enhancing neurocysticercosis lacking visible scolex, confirmed by PCR and sequencing on minicraniotomy brain tissue. All pathogen names, send-out ELISA, histology, and PCR findings excluded from case_prompt.
